title: Cyrus and the Sigil
premise: Theo Crane keeps the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in impossible things, while hiding a forbidden gift: the ability to speak with beasts. When a dying courier presses a map into Theo's hands, the guild's masked master, Cyrus, reveals the map charts the last dragon-fire — the ember that binds the covenant between the human realm and the beast-realm. Theo must choose between loyalty to the guild that sheltered them and the truth that Cyrus has been siphoning the fire to feed his own immortality. In the end, Theo reforges the covenant at terrible cost, spending their gift itself to reignite the flame, and the realms are saved while Theo is left voiceless to the beasts — until a dragonet's song answers them anyway.
about_author: Yara Reyes is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trade ledgers in port cities, an experience that taught her that every empire is built on paperwork and secrets. She writes fantasy about ordinary keepers of extraordinary things, and Cyrus and the Sigil is her second novel.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Theo Crane, POV. In the Vellum Guild's counting house, Theo balances accounts for caged griffins, bottled storms, and a sleeping river — all while concealing the beast-speaker gift that could get them culled. The emotional beat is quiet dread: a life of careful invisibility, and the loneliness of hiding who you are.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Salt Door
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. A bleeding courier collapses into the guild's back alley, pressing a scorched map into Theo's hands and gasping the word 'dragon-fire' before dying. Guild enforcers arrive seconds too late. The beat is panic and guilt — Theo hides the map, lying for the first time to the institution that raised them.

chapters.title: What the Rats Said
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Desperate for answers, Theo breaks their own rule and speaks with the guild's rats, learning the courier was hunted by something 'that wears a kind face.' The beat is vertigo: the hidden gift, used sparingly and guiltily, is now the only compass they have.

chapters.title: Master Cyrus Extends a Hand
chapters.summary: Theo and Cyrus, POV alternating. Cyrus — the guild's elegant, masked master — summons Theo, praising their discretion and offering promotion to 'special acquisitions.' Theo accepts, telling themselves loyalty and ambition are the same thing. The beat is seduction: power offered warmly, at precisely the moment of vulnerability.

chapters.title: The Map That Breathes
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Studying the map at night, Theo discovers it is drawn on dragon-skin and shifts to reveal a route only visible to someone who can hear beasts. A hawk outside the window warns: 'The masked one eats fire.' The beat is dread hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Special Acquisitions
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. On their first mission with enforcer Brannic, Theo witnesses a 'retrieval': a captured selkie sold to a collector, weeping in a crate. Theo realizes the guild's impossible things are stolen from the beast-realm. The beat is complicity — Theo signs the receipt, and hates themselves for it.

chapters.title: Brannic's Oath
chapters.summary: Brannic, POV. The enforcer, a guild orphan raised beside Theo, suspects the map exists and confronts Theo — not to betray them, but begging to be lied to so he can keep his clean conscience. The beat is aching loyalty: love expressed as a request for comfortable blindness.

chapters.title: Flight to the Cinder Coast
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo flees the guild with the map, guided by a half-tame fox and pursued by Cyrus's hounds. The fox's bitter commentary gives the journey both humor and heartbreak. The beat is exhilarating, terrified freedom — the first open sky of Theo's life.

chapters.title: The Beast-Realm's Edge
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. At the covenant-stone marking the border between realms, Theo meets Seraquin, an exiled beast-ambassador — an ancient wolf-woman who remembers the covenant's original terms. She confirms the fire is failing and names the price of renewal. The beat is awe shadowed by cost.

chapters.title: The Guttering Hearth
chapters.summary: Theo and Seraquin, POV. They reach the Cinder Coast and find the last dragon, Vaelith, barely alive, her flame the covenant's anchor — and find guild sigils carved into her chains. Cyrus has been bleeding the fire for decades. The beat is righteous fury meeting helplessness.

chapters.title: Terms of the Broken Covenant
chapters.summary: Seraquin, POV. In flashback-laced dialogue, Seraquin explains the covenant: realms survive by exchange, not theft, and reforging it requires a willing bearer to carry the sigil into the fire. Theo volunteers before hearing the full price. The beat is courage outrunning understanding.

chapters.title: What the Fox Knew
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. The fox, dying from a hound's wound, confesses it was once a man — a previous sigil-bearer who refused the fire. His deathbed warning: the sigil doesn't kill you; it takes the one thing you love most. The beat is grief as prophecy.

chapters.title: The Guild Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Brannic, POV. Brannic tracks Theo to the coast, ordered to retrieve the map or kill the bearer. Instead he defects, giving Theo his guild-ring as a key to Cyrus's vault. The beat is loyalty finally choosing truth — and knowing it may cost him everything.

chapters.title: Cyrus Unmasked
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. In his private sanctum, Cyrus removes the mask: beneath is a face burned smooth by centuries of borrowed fire. He remembers being a boy who watched dragons die and swore never to be powerless again. The beat is chilling sympathy — the villain as a survivor who never stopped surviving.

chapters.title: The Vault of Stolen Voices
chapters.summary: Theo and Brannic, POV. Using Brannic's ring, they infiltrate the guild vault, where Cyrus keeps bottled beast-voices, including — Theo realizes with horror — a recording of their own mother, a beast-speaker the guild 'processed' years ago. The beat is personal devastation weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: The Trap of Kind Faces
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Cyrus corners them, offering a bargain: the mother's voice restored, the gift kept secret, a life of comfort — if Theo hands over the map. For one terrible moment Theo wants to say yes. The beat is temptation at its most human.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo refuses — 'a voice bought with a realm's silence is just another cage' — and escapes with Brannic as the guild burns its own archives to erase the evidence. The mother's bottle shatters in the fire; her last whisper is the covenant's opening line. The beat is loss transfigured into inheritance.

chapters.title: The Long Dark of the Ember Road
chapters.summary: Theo, Brannic, and Seraquin, POV alternating. The three race the dying fire back to the Cinder Coast through a land already failing — rivers forgetting to flow, beasts going silent. The beat is apocalyptic quiet: the world ending not with violence but with forgetting.

chapters.title: Vaelith's Choice
chapters.summary: Vaelith, POV. The last dragon, freed from her chains by Brannic, reveals she could reignite the fire alone — by burning the beast-realm's memories to fuel it. She asks Theo to carry the sigil instead, so both realms keep their pasts. The beat is humility: even dragons must ask.

chapters.title: Cyrus at the Hearth
chapters.summary: Theo and Cyrus, POV. Cyrus arrives for the final confrontation, no longer masked, offering to share the fire 'fairly' — a lie even he believes. Theo and Brannic hold the hearth-stone against him while Vaelith prepares. The beat is the climax: fists, fire, and Theo speaking the covenant's true name aloud.

chapters.title: The Sigil Reforged
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo takes the sigil into the flame, paying the price — the gift itself — and the covenant blazes renewed across both realms. Cyrus, offered a place in the new order, instead walks into the fire he can no longer steal. The beat is sacrifice and terrible, necessary peace.

chapters.title: A Voice in the Ash
chapters.summary: Theo, POV, epilogue. Months later, Theo keeps honest ledgers in a rebuilt guild, voiceless to beasts, with Brannic at their side. Then a dragonet — Vaelith's firstborn — lands on the counting-house roof and sings, and Theo hears it. The beat is grace: what was given up returns, changed and chosen.
